Agent Name: Planner
, Step Number: 1
, Reason for Mistake: The Planner incorrectly identified mirrors as the best example of light refraction. Refraction is the bending of light as it passes through a transparent medium (like the glass in eyeglasses), whereas mirrors primarily function by reflecting light off a surface. While surface imperfections on a mirror might cause some scattering, their defining optical property is reflection, not refraction. Eyeglasses (lenses) are the standard textbook example of an object designed specifically to refract light.
